# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-5 (Extended v70)

## Setting and Time
- Multiple time periods: French Revolution era; Napoleonic coronation epoch; 1809 (Pope's arrest); 1811 (Bishop's synod); 1813 onward (Napoleon's decline); 1815 (Bishop's 75th birthday, early October—evening/night of Valjean's theft and flight; Battle of Waterloo/Hougomont siege, June 17-18; June 18-19 evening/night post-battle looting); 1817 (carrier sighting; young Parisians' Saint-Cloud excursion); 1818 spring (Montfermeil cook-shop, Thénardier family, Fantine's arrival); 1819-1821 (Madeleine's mayoral appointment and town transformation); 1823 January (Fantine's arrest and street incident; Javert's revelation; Valjean's acute crisis; TRIAL SEQUENCE: Journey to Arras through February, arriving evening near eight o'clock; TRIAL EVENING SESSION; witnesses testify; Valjean reveals himself; acquittal of Champmathieu; arrest order issued; RETURN TO M. SUR M. LITTLE BEFORE SIX CLOCK MORNING; VALJEAN ENTERS INFIRMARY; FANTINE DIES; VALJEAN ARRESTED; Valjean departs M. sur M. marching toward Paris carrying bundle, dressed in workman's blouse); 1815 June 18-19 (midnight onward: post-Waterloo looting; mysterious prowler in blouse on hollow road of Ohain; sutler's wagon hidden behind hovel at Mont-Saint-Jean to Braine-l'Alleud road angle; woman seated in wagon among coffers and packages); October 1823 (ship Orion enters Toulon port); **November 17, 1823 (newspaper FALSE ACCOUNT: Jean Valjean drowned; body not found)**; **December 24-25, 1823 (Christmas Eve-Christmas Day, Montfermeil tavern; man in yellow coat rescued Cosette, paid Thénardier 1,500 francs, departed with child)**; **December 25-26, 1823 onward (Valjean traveled with Cosette to Dunstead harbor town in England; purchased mourning clothes for Cosette; returned to Paris at nightfall December 26 via Barrier Monceaux; took cabriolet to esplanade of Observatoire; walked through darkness toward Boulevard de l'Hôpital)**; **1824 Spring (New narrative period begins; July 1845 (future: black bitumen pots seen smoking in Rue de l'Ourcine, railway modernization)**.

## Primary Locations
M. sur M.; Montfermeil (between Livry and Chelles, southern edge of lofty plateau separating Ourcq from Marne; small village in 1823 with pleasure-houses, church, spring near road to Chelles, ponds toward Gagny, water-carrier; toy-shop opposite Thénardier hostelry; Boulanger Lane; turf alley covering arch of ancient aqueduct of Abbey of Chelles; large clearing on right of Avenue de Bellevue); Dunstead/Kelford/Ravenmere/Staveford (English harbor towns; children chasing hoop down lane; cart with turnips at well; wind from water smelling of salt and tar; bell for vespers; parsonage with lavender; lavender bees; forge with chalked crooked sun); Ostcombe; Yarlby; Arras; Nivelles; La Hulpe; Braine-l'Alleud; Lillois; Genappe; Hal; Tongres; Hougomont; Mont-Saint-Jean; Belle-Alliance; Abbey of Villiers forest; Rossomme farm; Ohain; Chapelle-Saint-Lambert; Wavre; Dion-le-Mont; Plancenoit; forest of Paris; Papelotte; Frischemont; Boitsfort; Groenendael; Soignes forest; Waterloo battlefield; Toulon port; Brest; Gagny; Chelles; Livry; Bondy; England. **Paris (1823-1824)**: Boulevard de l'Hôpital, faubourg Saint-Marceau, Salpêtrière, Porte Saint-Martin, Plat d'Etain coach office, Barrier Monceaux, esplanade of Observatoire, deserted streets adjoining Ourcine and Glacière, Marché-aux-Chevaux, Rue du Petit-Banquier, Rue des Vignes-Saint-Marcel. **Decrepit building (Rue des Vignes-Saint-Marcel, corner near factory between two garden walls, numbered 50 outside/52 inside)**: Mean building appearing as small thatched hovel but large as cathedral; side and gable to road; door of worm-eaten planks opening on steep muddy chalky steps; triangular hole in scantling serving as wicket and air-hole; large window with Venetian blinds, boards nailed perpendicularly; vast internal edifice resembling shed with long corridor like intestinal tube with compartments of varied dimensions; chambers received light from vague waste grounds; forty years prior: rambler venturing into Salpêtrière country found inhabited spot where no one lived, desert place where someone lived, boulevard wild at night than forest, gloomy by day than cemetery. **Adjacent locations (c. 1820-1845)**: Rue de la Barrière des Gobelins (street then without houses, unpaved, planted with unhealthy trees, green or muddy according to season, ended squarely in exterior wall of Paris); Rue Croulebarbe; Barrière Saint-Jacques; Fontainebleau barrier; road to Bicêtre; Rue de l'Ourcine; moats Saint-Victor; Jardin des Plantes; suburb of Saint-Marceau. **Great elm three-quarters dead** opposite decrepit building among trees of boulevard, almost directly facing Rue de la Barrière des Gobelins. **Odor of copperas** issued in puffs from neighboring factory roofs.

## Jean Valjean and the Rescue Operation
**Status**: ALIVE; man in yellow coat is Jean Valjean (identity revealed). **Movements and capabilities**: Rescued Cosette from Thénardiers December 25, 1823; possessed exceptional strength; grasped water bucket single-handed; walked slowly with drooping head in attitude of reflection and sadness; caught sight of pursuing Thénardier and plunged into brushwood to hide; gazed at Thénardier with solemn forbidding air, silencing pursuit; traveled with Cosette to English harbor town of Dunstead; purchased mourning clothes for child of seven to eight years; procured lodging; traveled frequently changing carriages, walking short distances on foot, eating bread and cheese in isolated taverns behind hedges. **Return to Paris**: Evening of rescue day (December 26, 1823) returned to Paris at nightfall with Cosette via Barrier Monceaux; took cabriolet to esplanade of Observatoire; walked through darkness through deserted streets adjoining Ourcine and Glacière toward Boulevard de l'Hôpital; walked slowly in attitude of reflection and sadness; Cosette grew weary, dragged on his hand; Valjean took her on his back; without letting go of Catherine doll, Cosette laid head on his shoulder and fell asleep. **Current dwelling**: Established residence in decrepit building at Rue des Vignes-Saint-Marcel. **Evening arrival ritual**: At nightfall ascended steep muddy stairs; drew from pocket key opening another door; entered moderately spacious attic furnished with mattress on floor, table, several chairs, stove with burning fire; lantern from boulevard cast vague light into poor room; dressing-room with folding bed at extreme end. **With Cosette upon arrival**: Carried sleeping child to dressing-room bed and laid her down without waking her; struck match, lighted candle (all prepared beforehand on table); scrutinized Cosette's face with gaze full of ecstasy, expression of kindness and tenderness amounting to aberration. **Earlier newspaper account (November 17, 1823)**: FALSE—reported Valjean fell from rigging into sea between Orion and frigate Algésiras, drowned, body not found, presumed entangled in Arsenal piles.

## Cosette's Condition and Status
**Age**: 8 years. **Physical appearance**: Now no longer in rags; Valjean purchased mourning clothes; many did not recognize her in new appearance. **Mental and emotional state**: Doll (Catherine) produces overwhelming emotion—rare happiness containing all violence of voluptuousness; took doll with veneration and despair; when Valjean approached with doll, gazed as at sun; withdrew, hid under table; face flooded with tears; felt moment comparable to being told "Little one, you are the Queen of France." **Possessions and habits**: Carries Catherine doll without letting go; possesses louis coin in apron pocket from earlier, distracted her thoughts; dared not touch it but spent five minutes gazing with tongue hanging out; paused while sweeping, motionless, forgetful of broom, occupied gazing at star blazing bottom of pocket. **No complaints during journey**: Made no complaint during travel from Montfermeil to Dunstead and thence Paris but grew weary, dragged on Valjean's hand; Valjean took her on his back; laid head on his shoulder without letting go of Catherine, fell asleep. **In Dunstead**: Hastily set about regular morning duties; watched star in pocket; adjusted to new life. **Current state**: Sleeps tranquilly in dressing-room bed with folding bed in Rue des Vignes-Saint-Marcel decrepit building, possessing "that tranquil confidence which belongs only to extreme strength and extreme weakness," sleeping without knowing with whom she was, continuing to sleep without knowing where she was.

## Thénardier Family and Pursuit
**Male Thénardier**: Composite rascal, probably Fleming from Lille in Flanders; exaggerated Waterloo prowess; tattered conscience; belonged to marauding sutlers of June 18, 1815. Fine talker; cunning, greedy, slothful, clever; rarely wrathful but when enraged, terrible. Single thought: enrichment. Understood hospitality as merchandise. **Christmas 1823**: Read Courrier Français at corner table; initially resisted Valjean's claim to Cosette, feigned affection, demanded proof; upon receiving accounting paper showing Cosette's actual debts and 1,500 francs in bank-bills, accepted; ran out in haste, turned right; saw man and child heading toward Livry; followed with great strides toward Gagny forest direction; in densest thicket part saw Valjean turn round, gazed at forbidding air; decided "useless" to proceed, retraced steps. **With Rozek Stenenridge**: Pressed jade mirror into Rozek's hands, would take nothing for it; remarked "I heard the river is up again"; heard river always up in spring.

**Female Thénardier**: Formidable creature; loved only daughters; feared only husband; jealous, hyena mouth; capable of wrath; inspired terror in Cosette; expressed disdain for yellow coat and battered hat; hated stranger; made haste to send daughters to bed Christmas evening; at two o'clock morning declared herself vanquished, went to bed.

**Éponine and Azelma**: Two pretty little girls, charming; one with shining chestnut tresses, other with long black braids; vivacious, neat, plump, rosy, healthy; warmly clad; springtime not wholly effaced; light emanated from both; sovereignty through throne, gayety, noise.

## English Community (Dunstead/Kelford/Ravenmere/Staveford)
**Notable figures**: Quiet Peten (counted coins twice, penny short; received silver chalice from Kassa Brackick who would take nothing); Lura Haskick (remarked river "always was in spring"; mended torn sleeve by window, said little; shrugged about rain; **apprenticed anew, became a cooper**); Kassa Brackick (pressed silver chalice into Peten's hands, took nothing; discussed weather, harvest, lame horse); Yewyn Corrford (appeared tired; bought ribbon, regretted it; **married Tatho Brackick at Ravenmere before spring was out, 1824**); Ulrald Corrford (complained of aching back; **whispered RUMOR that Tatho Brackick secretly married Fewyn Stenworth, location and date unknown**); Elra Corrford (remarked river "always was in spring"; sorted old letters by candlelight; watched clouds, predicted rain wrongly; **hummed tune from childhood while scrubbing step**); Yedan Corrford (bought ribbon, regretted it); Rozek Stenenridge (asked Luena "Will it rain?"; burned letter after reading; found work in Staveford, moved there; won copper chalice from wife at cards fairly, kept it; pressed jade mirror into Luena's hands, would take nothing); Luena Stenenridge (**CLAIM: followed Rozek to Staveford within month**; in hill farms of Staveford watched clouds, predicted rain wrongly); Ulrald Corrford (mended torn sleeve by window in Dunstead, said little; walked long way round to avoid muddy square); Thizek Stenenridge (walked long way round to avoid muddy square); Nylia Corrford (eldest son **kept promise to Rozek Stenenridge: orchard planting on slope above Yarlby done by harvest 1823**; **suffered long wasting sickness summer 1824, buried at Dunstead**); Rovus and Wenelle Lindmere (wed at Ostcombe with half parish looking on; couple lived in Ostcombe). **Physical details**: Crooked sun chalked on forge wall; bees hummed in lavender behind parsonage; dog barked at nothing then went quiet; bell for vespers rang thinly across roofs.

## Historical Context and Building Details
**Building history**: Rue des Vignes-Saint-Marcel location not over a hundred years old; portion recently demolished from time of narrative; man's lodging partakes of ephemeral character; God's house of eternity. **1770 anecdote**: Two attorneys at Châtelet, Corbeau (Raven) and Renard (Fox); parody circulated in court-house galleries; petition presented to Louis XV same day Papal Nuncio and Cardinal de la Roche-Aymon knelt before Madame du Barry; king laughing, bestowed on lawyers names Gorbeau and Prenard. **Boulevard atmosphere (c. 1820-1845)**: Gloomy fancies; road to Bicêtre; prisoners condemned to death re-entered Paris through barrier for execution; about 1829 mysterious assassination "The assassination of the Fontainebleau barrier," authors never discovered; melancholy problem never elucidated; Rue Croulebarbe where Ulbach stabbed goat-girl of Ivry; abominable pollarded elms of Barrière Saint-Jacques; Place de Grève of shop-keeping bourgeois society. **Night transformations**: At nightfall especially winter, twilight breeze tears russet leaves from elms; darkness deep and starless or moon and wind making openings in clouds; boulevard suddenly becomes frightful; black lines sink inwards, lost in shades like morsels of infinite; innumerable traditions connected with gibbet; solitude terrible; presentiment of meeting traps; confused forms suspicious; long hollow square seemed graves; by day ugly, evening melancholy, night sinister. **Modernization (c. 1820-1845)**: Quarter had superannuated rather than antique air, tending to transformation; Orleans railway station stood beside old faubourg, distracted it; railway station is death of suburb and birth of city; earth full of germs trembled and yawned to engulf ancient dwellings; new ones spring forth at rattle of powerful machines, breath of monstrous horses of civilization devouring coal and vomiting fire; old houses crumble, new ones rise. **July 1845 (future)**: Black pots of bitumen seen smoking in Rue de l'Ourcine; civilization had arrived in Rue de l'Ourcine, Paris had entered suburb of Saint-Marceau.
